title: Queen Vashti Deposed

questions.question: Over how many provinces did King Ahasuerus reign?
questions.explanation: Esther 1:1 (ESV): "...who reigned from India to Ethiopia over 127 provinces..."

questions.question: In which citadel was the king’s throne located?
questions.explanation: Esther 1:2 (ESV): "...when King Ahasuerus sat on his royal throne in Susa the citadel..."

questions.question: How long did the feast for the officials and servants last?
Who gave a feast for the women in the palace?
questions.explanation: Esther 1:9 (ESV): "Queen Vashti also gave a feast for the women in the palace that belonged to King Ahasuerus."

questions.question: Why did the king summons Queen Vashti?
options: To show her beauty to the people and princes
questions.correctAnswer: To show her beauty to the people and princes
questions.explanation: Esther 1:11 (ESV): "...in order to show the peoples and the princes her beauty, for she was lovely to look at."

questions.question: What was the king’s reaction when Vashti refused to come?
options: He was enraged and his anger burned within him
questions.correctAnswer: He was enraged and his anger burned within him
questions.explanation: Esther 1:12 (ESV): "...At this the king became enraged, and his anger burned within him."

questions.question: Who did the king consult regarding the law and justice?
options: The wise men who knew the times
questions.correctAnswer: The wise men who knew the times
questions.explanation: Esther 1:13 (ESV): "Then the king said to the wise men who knew the times..."

questions.question: Which of the seven princes answered the king regarding Vashti?
questions.explanation: Esther 1:16 (ESV): "Then Memucan said in the presence of the king and the officials..."

questions.question: According to Memucan, whom did Vashti wrong?
options: The king, all the officials, and all the peoples
questions.correctAnswer: The king, all the officials, and all the peoples
questions.explanation: Esther 1:16 (ESV): "...Not only to the king has Queen Vashti done wrong, but also to all the officials and all the peoples..."

questions.question: What was the predicted result of the queen’s behavior on other women?
options: They would look with contempt on their husbands
questions.correctAnswer: They would look with contempt on their husbands
questions.explanation: Esther 1:17 (ESV): "...causing them to look with contempt on their husbands..."

questions.question: What material were the couches at the feast made of?
questions.explanation: Esther 1:6 (ESV): "...couches of gold and silver on a mosaic pavement..."

questions.question: What was unique about the drinking vessels?
options: They were of gold, and no two were alike
questions.correctAnswer: They were of gold, and no two were alike
questions.explanation: Esther 1:7 (ESV): "Drinks were served in golden vessels, vessels of different kinds..."

questions.question: What was the rule concerning drinking at the feast?
options: It was according to the law; no one was compelled
questions.correctAnswer: It was according to the law; no one was compelled
questions.explanation: Esther 1:8 (ESV): "And drinking was according to this edict: 'There is no compulsion.'"

questions.question: How many eunuchs attended the king?
questions.explanation: Esther 1:10 (ESV): "...he commanded... the seven eunuchs who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus..."

questions.question: How were the letters sent to the provinces written?
options: To each province in its own script and to each people in its own language
questions.correctAnswer: To each province in its own script and to each people in its own language
questions.explanation: Esther 1:22 (ESV): "He sent letters... to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language..."

key_verse_text: If it please the king, let a royal order go out from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes so that it may not be repealed, that Vashti is never again to come before King Ahasuerus. And let the king give her royal position to another who is better than she.
